title: DevOps Roadmap
description: A curated, stage-by-stage path from Git and Linux basics through containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and the major cloud platforms.
audience: Developers who deploy their own code today and want the skills that make shipping reliable and repeatable.
intro: DevOps is broad but not deep everywhere. This roadmap gives you a solid general foundation first, then lets you specialize in the cloud your target jobs actually use.

stages.title: Git & Linux Workflow
stages.description: Every DevOps tool assumes you are comfortable in a terminal and a Git repository. Master the daily developer workflow before adding infrastructure on top.
stages.milestone: You can manage branches and rebases confidently, and navigate, debug, and script a Linux shell without anxiety.

steps.note: These skills pay off every single working day — do not rush through them.

stages.title: Containers & Orchestration
stages.description: Docker packages an application with its dependencies; Kubernetes runs many of those packages reliably. Together they are the core of modern infrastructure.
stages.milestone: You can containerize an application, compose services together, and explain what Kubernetes manages on your behalf.

steps.note: The Docker and Kubernetes modules are the heart of this stage — run the labs, do not just read.
Your quick reference once the container modules are done.

stages.title: Cloud Foundations
stages.description: Pick one major cloud and learn its core building blocks — compute, storage, networking, and identity. Depth in one beats surface-level knowledge of both.
stages.milestone: You can deploy a containerized application to your chosen cloud and reason about cost, networking, and identity basics.

steps.note: Choose AWS or Azure as your primary based on your job market; treat the other as secondary.
Skim this after AWS if your workplace uses Azure — most concepts map across.

stages.title: Hands-On Practice
stages.description: Cloud skills only stick when you build under realistic constraints. Work through end-to-end scenarios that mix services the way real projects do.
stages.milestone: You can take a small application and deploy it end-to-end — container, database, and identity — on your chosen cloud without a walkthrough.

steps.note: Even on AWS, these scenarios build the transferable cloud reasoning that interviews test.

stages.title: Interview Preparation
stages.description: Consolidate with a question bank focused on pipelines: how code gets from a commit to production, and how teams keep that path safe.
stages.milestone: You can design a CI/CD pipeline for a typical web application and explain each stage's purpose and failure modes.
